Bridge

Backwards: Unit 4 (Tidy data in the tidyverse) built the aggregation this unit formalises, and Unit 5 (EDA and the grammar of graphics) found the anomalies the data card now records; Unit 3 downloaded the raw snapshot and explains the ChEMBL schema (Python edition). Forwards: Units 11 and 12 consume this table and implement the scaffold split argued for in Section 7 (supervised workflow, validation); Unit 17 builds on the noise estimate of Section 4 (uncertainty and applicability domain); Unit 21 analyses the periodontitis series whose metadata we inspected here (omics); and Unit 23 turns the data card into the reporting standards a journal expects (scientific communication). The R-edition index lists every unit and the Python edition of this unit runs the same protocol with RDKit. Sister courses: the chemistry of standardisation and curation is developed in Unit 4 and Unit 7 of the cheminformatics course, scaffold-based chemical space in its Unit 8 and validation practice in its Unit 14; the machine-learning consequences of a leaking split are covered in Model evaluation of the AI course.

10. Summary

  • Quality is fitness for a stated purpose, and splits into correctness, precision, representativeness and documentation. Treat them separately; only the first is what most people mean by “cleaning”.
  • Write the protocol as tested code with reason codes. Four testthat tests guard the framework; the pipeline excluded 44 of 5,089 records (0.9%) — 3 without a structure, 13 carrying ChEMBL’s validity flag (including one impossible IC50 of exactly 0 nM), 26 with no numeric value, 2 outside the heavy-atom window — and reproduced the reference table exactly: 4,280 compounds, identical censoring flags, identical scaffolds, potencies agreeing to 0.0005 log units.
  • Estimate the noise from your own replicates. Seven hundred and eighty inter-document pairs give σ ≈ 0.506 log units, matching the published ≈0.5 for public bioactivity data; IC50 and Ki values for the same compound differ by −0.87 log units on average.
  • Convert the noise into a budget. With σ = 0.506 and an observed spread of 1.108, the reliability is 0.792: no model can exceed R² ≈ 0.79 or beat RMSE ≈ 0.51 against these labels, and a perfect classifier agrees with a noisy label only 84–87% of the time.
  • The activity threshold is a decision. Active-to-inactive goes 2.19 → 0.91 → 0.49 across 6.0 / 6.5 / 7.0; the active set narrows from 802 to 366 scaffolds; 984 compounds (36%) change class; 1,011 sit within one σ of the 6.5 cut. Report the sensitivity.
  • Diagnose the concentration. 1,453 of 2,005 scaffolds are singletons (Gini 0.47), seven of 222 documents supply half the measurements (Gini 0.82), and a random split leaves 65% of test compounds with a relative in training against 0% for a scaffold split.
  • Flag, do not silently delete. 210 property alerts (4.9%) are recorded in the table; they are weaker and more often censored than the rest, so deleting them would remove part of the potency range rather than clean it.
  • When the rows are people the rules change. The GEO metadata we inspected carry no demographic quasi-identifiers at all — minimisation at collection beats generalisation afterwards — and k-anonymity, l-diversity, ethics approval, consent and the applicable data-protection law are prerequisites, not paperwork.
  • Ship a data card. Generate it from the analysis so it cannot go stale.

11. Self-assessment

  1. Why must structure standardisation precede de-duplication?

Because the same molecule is deposited in several forms — free base, salt, hydrate, charged species — each with its own database identifier. De-duplicating on the identifier leaves those as separate compounds (ripasudil would appear three times in this dataset). Standardising first collapses them to one canonical parent whose InChIKey is the de-duplication key.

  1. A reviewer asks why you removed 13 records. What do you show them?

The log line with its reason code (E03, “ChEMBL data_validity_comment flag”), the stored excluded rows, and the observation that twelve are potencies between 120 µM and 30 mM and one is an IC50 of exactly 0 nM whose logarithm is infinite. A curation step you cannot justify record by record is a step you should not have taken.

  1. How do you estimate experimental uncertainty without repeating any experiment?

Use the replicates already in the data. For compounds measured in two different documents, take each document’s mean and form the difference; if each is the truth plus independent noise of standard deviation σ, the differences have standard deviation σ√2, so σ = √(mean squared difference / 2). Here 780 pairs give σ ≈ 0.506 log units. Pairs from the same document are not independent and must be excluded.

  1. Your classifier reaches 96% accuracy on a public bioactivity benchmark. What do you check first?

The split and the labels. With this dataset’s noise, a perfect model agrees with the label only about 86% of the time, so 96% means either information has leaked between training and test (duplicate structures, salt forms, a random split with 65% scaffold overlap) or the test set is unrepresentative. Check de-duplication at InChIKey level first, then re-evaluate under a scaffold split.

  1. What exactly is the reliability of a dataset, and why is it the right baseline?

Reliability is the fraction of the observed variance that is true signal rather than measurement noise: σ²true/σ²obs = 1 − σ²/σ²obs, here 0.792. It is the right baseline because a model is scored against noisy observations, so even a perfect predictor of the truth cannot explain the noise component. Reporting R² against 0 flatters the model; reporting it against the ceiling says how much of the available signal was captured.

  1. Why report threshold sensitivity instead of choosing the best threshold?

Because the threshold creates the classes rather than discovering them: the active-to-inactive ratio moves from 2.19 to 0.49 across the three conventional cuts, and 36% of compounds change class. Choosing the threshold that maximises your metric is tuning on the outcome. Report all three, or model the continuous value.

  1. What is analogue bias, and which diagnostic reveals it?

The dataset is dominated by families of close structural relatives, because it records optimisation campaigns rather than a sample of chemical space. The diagnostics are the scaffold count and its concentration — 2,005 scaffolds for 4,280 compounds, 72% singletons, Gini 0.47, largest family 214 — and the direct measurement of split leakage: 65% of a random test set has a scaffold relative in training.

  1. A scaffold split lowers your reported R² by 0.2. Is the model worse?

No; the earlier number was wrong. The random split rewarded recognising known families, which is not the task. The scaffold-split number estimates performance on chemistry the model has not seen, which is what a prospective application needs. Note also that a scaffold split moves whole families and so disturbs the class balance between train and test, making the estimate noisier — report both the score and the split.

  1. Should compounds flagged by a structural or property alert be removed from a training set?

Not automatically. PAINS filters flag substructures associated with assay interference but have well-documented false positives, and several approved drugs match them; a rule-of-five alert, like the one computed here, flags only that a molecule is large or greasy. Flag them in the table, report the count (210 here, 4.9%), inspect them if they are influential, and state what you did. In this dataset the flagged compounds are weaker and more often censored than the rest, so removing them would truncate the potency range.

  1. Distinguish a direct identifier, a quasi-identifier and a sensitive attribute, with an example of each.

A direct identifier names the person (national identity number). A quasi-identifier identifies them only in combination or by linkage (date of birth, postcode, sex). A sensitive attribute is what the study is about and must not be disclosed (a periodontitis diagnosis, a genotype). Protection works on the quasi-identifiers: removing or generalising them is what makes the sensitive attribute safe to publish.

  1. The GEO metadata we examined have no age or sex column. Is that good practice or a limitation?

Both, and the trade-off should be explicit. It removes the quasi-identifiers that drive re-identification risk, so the series can be public, but it also removes genuine confounders for periodontitis, so the data cannot support an adjusted analysis. The right response is to state the limitation in the data card rather than to wish the fields were there.

  1. What belongs in a data card that does not belong in a paper’s methods section?

The negative and operational information: what the dataset must not be used for, the known biases with numbers, the measured uncertainty and the performance ceiling it implies, the licence, the exclusion counts by reason code, and the version and date. A methods section describes what you did; a data card tells the next person what they can safely do.

Glossary

Analogue bias
Over-representation of families of close structural relatives, because the data record optimisation campaigns rather than a sample of chemical space.
Curation log
A per-step record of a cleaning pipeline: reason code, description, records removed, records remaining. The basis of a flow diagram and a data card.
Data card
A short structured document shipped with a dataset: purpose, provenance, composition, exclusions, known biases, recommended and discouraged uses.
Direct identifier / quasi-identifier / sensitive attribute
A field that names a person; a field that identifies them in combination or by linkage; the field the study is about and that must not be disclosed.
Gini coefficient
A measure of concentration between 0 (perfectly even) and 1 (all in one group); used here for scaffold families and source documents.
k-anonymity
A release in which every combination of quasi-identifiers is shared by at least k records, so no record is distinguishable from fewer than k−1 others.
Noise ceiling (reliability)
The fraction of observed variance that is true signal, 1 − σ²/σ²obs; the maximum R² any model can reach against those labels.
PAINS
Pan-assay interference compounds: substructures associated with apparent activity in many unrelated assays. A flag for review, not a deletion rule.
Pseudonymisation / anonymisation
Replacing identifiers with a code while a re-identification key exists (still personal data in law) versus removing the possibility of re-identification altogether.
Reason code
A short stable label attached to every excluded record, so any exclusion can be audited later.
Scaffold split
A train/test split that assigns whole Bemis–Murcko scaffold families to one side, so no test compound has a structural relative in training.
Threshold sensitivity
How class balance, composition and reported performance change when the activity cut-off is moved; a required part of any classification report on continuous data.
